extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of literature; readers studying authors and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading and evaluating the works and styles of various American (and related) authors; includes specific questions, comparative prompts, and stylistic/ thematic criteria to consider when analyzing an author's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiographical element
rubrics_metrics.description: The autobiographical element in Mr. Anderson's work is marked and should never be forgotten in judging his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging Anderson, always note how much of the work is autobiographical; the conventional element may be 'patched on,' particularly in longer works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of literary traditions and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of literary traditions and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the qualities to note in Anderson (and similar authors) is how independent their methods are from established literary traditions; observe departures from convention as a strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keen eye for details
rubrics_metrics.description: A keen eye for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study examples where precise, detailed description contributes to characterization or atmosphere; use these passages as models of detail-management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passionate desire to interpret life
rubrics_metrics.description: A passionate desire to interpret life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the author's urgency to interpret experience shapes narrative choices and thematic emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuing individual, seemingly unimportant lives
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong sense of the value of individual lives of little seeming importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note how the author elevates ordinary lives; examine whether this valuation yields insight or sentimentality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosing defects: experience vs temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Are Mr. Anderson's defects due to the limitations of his experience, or do you notice certain temperamental defects which he is not likely to outgrow?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When critiquing an author, distinguish between flaws traceable to limited material/experience and those likely rooted in temperament or temperament-driven habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentation in form and use of poetic cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Anderson's experiments in form are interesting to study. Compare the prosiness of his verse with his efforts to use poetic cadence in The Triumph of the Egg. Does it suggest to you the possibility of developing a form intermediate between prose and free verse?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze attempts to blend prose and poetic techniques; compare verse and prose passages, look for cadence, lineation, and rhythmic devices that suggest hybrid forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific success (novelist vs short-story writer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Mr. Anderson succeed best as novelist or as short-story writer? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate an author's effectiveness across forms; identify strengths and weaknesses particular to novel-length vs short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative reading to illuminate merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Mr. Beebe is preëminently an ornithologist, he belongs to literature by reason of the volumes of nature studies listed below. A comparison of his books with those of the English ornithologist, W.H. Hudson ... is illuminative of the merits of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use side-by-side comparison with similar writers to highlight distinctive strengths and weaknesses; comparisons with contemporaries or near-contemporaries can clarify an author's place and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative description analysis (genre-specific comparisons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Another interesting comparison may be made between Mr. Beebe's descriptions of the jungle in Jungle Peace and H.M. Tomlinson's in Sea and Jungle (cf. Manly and Rickert).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the same subject treated by different authors to analyze differences in approach, tone, sensory detail, and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of suggestion to appeal to the senses
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of the use of suggestion in appeal to the different senses brings out one of the main sources of Mr. Beebe's charm as a writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading, isolate examples where suggestion (implied detail, hinted imagery) engages sight, sound, smell, touch, and taste; assess how suggestion versus explicit description functions aesthetically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose rhythm observation by reading aloud
rubrics_metrics.description: Read aloud several fine passages to observe the prose rhythms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To perceive an author's rhythmic effects, read passages aloud; note cadence, sentence length variation, and musicality that may be less obvious on silent reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand an author's declared theory before reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Before reading Mr. Cabell's stories, read his Beyond Life, which explains his theory of romance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with an author's theoretical statements or manifestos to contextualize and interpret their fiction; theory often illuminates recurring motifs and structural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify an author's major divisions/themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Cabell's fiction falls into two divisions: (1) Romances of the middle ages. (2) Comedies of present-day Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify major thematic or generic divisions in an author's oeuvre; use these categories to organize comparative and historical readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of archaism, artifice, and historical atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: He has created an imaginary province ... His effort to create mediæval atmosphere by the use of archaisms does not preclude modern idiom and slang. ... The artifice is more apparent than the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the balance between archaism/artifice and authenticity: do archaisms and invented sources produce convincing atmosphere or expose artifice? Consider effects on immersion and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify admired and disparaged influences to deduce qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolate the authors for whom Mr. Cabell expresses particular admiration and those for whom he expresses contempt in Beyond Life and deduce from his attitudes his peculiar literary qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an author's stated influences (likes and dislikes) as clues to recurrent stylistic and thematic tendencies in their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style elements: rhythm, avoidance of clichés, archaic diction, allusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Cabell's style is notable for the elaboration of its rhythm, its careful avoidance of clichés, its preference for rare, archaic words and its allusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze diction (archaic/rare words), rhythmic elaboration, allusions, and cliché-avoidance as components of style; judge whether these features serve clarity, charm, or artificiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate style by sincerity, simplicity, clarity, and charm
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider it from the point of view of sincerity, simplicity, clarity, and charm. Does it intensify or dull your interest in what he has to say?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply criteria of sincerity, simplicity, clarity, and charm to stylistic judgments: do stylistic choices enhance communication and engagement or obscure it?

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he a definite philosophy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author advances or embodies a coherent underlying philosophy that shapes themes, character behavior, and narrative outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he a genuine sense of character or do his characters repeat the same personality?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the author's skill in creating distinct, varied characters rather than iterations of a single type; check for psychological depth and differentiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity vs self-conscious mannerism
rubrics_metrics.description: Is he a sincere artist or 'a self-conscious attitudinizer?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine artistic voice from mannered, self-conscious poses; look for signs of affectation or recurring theatrical postures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary reputation and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Is he likely ever to hold the high place in American literature which by some critics is denied him today? If so, on what basis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging an author's lasting significance, articulate the specific bases (philosophy, technique, characterization, originality) that might justify enduring status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of detail and picture-making language
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Bodenheim gets his effects by his management of detail. For this reason, his use of picture-making words and suggestive phrases offers material for special study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how selective details and evocative phrases produce effects; extract model passages for lessons in economy of detail and imagistic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider realism, objectivity (detachment), and sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Miss Cather's special field is the pioneer life of immigrants in the Middle West. Points to be considered are: (1) her realism; (2) her detachment or objectivity; (3) her sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading Cather (and similar writers), evaluate the balance among realistic representation, authorial detachment/objectivity, and sympathetic engagement with subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the value of material
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the value of her material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the subject matter itself (settings, social milieux, historical moments) offers sufficient interest, complexity, and relevance to sustain literary treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative grouping to situate an author
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare her studies with those of Cahan, Cournos, and Tobenkin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place an author in relation to peers who treat similar themes or communities to understand distinguishing approaches and contributions.
